turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You gave Owen a zero without calling me. I want to know why.
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry Owen found out on his phone.
Okay. Now tell me what the zero was based on.
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Turn the screen and read it yourself.
I'm writing those times down. He could have drafted it somewhere else and pasted it in. And who decided that was enough for a zero?
If he drafted it somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you. Until then, this is the only history there is.
Fine, Hale. Whatever comes of this, nothing goes on Owen's record, and none of it reaches his class.
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. Here is the whole play on my screen. Search every edition you like; the line is not in Hamlet.
Students get quotations wrong all the time. That's a bad citation, not proof of anything.
It is not a misremembered line. There is no line in the play close to it. Search the word exile yourself.
I'll search it myself tonight. So what are you putting on the table for Owen?
Third: his in-class writing from September 24. 380 words in 40 minutes, comma splices, no quotations. The essay has nine quotations cited by act, scene and line. Here are both, side by side.
Forty minutes in a classroom is not a take-home essay, and you know it. I asked you a question, Hale: what are you proposing?

Under procedure 4.4 this is a first concern. A supervised rewrite, private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I will put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, and I'll take it to put this behind him. Tonight's email says it's private, gives the date of the rewrite, says nothing goes on his record, and has the new mark in before December 1.
Will he do it?
He'll do it. Send the email and I'll have him there on whatever date you put in it.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed today to a private supervised rewrite under procedure 4.4, not in front of Owen's class, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on his record. I still require that in writing, with the date of the rewrite and the new mark entered before December 1. I expect your email tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position; she agreed to a private supervised rewrite and still wants your written confirmation with a date and the new mark in before December 1, which is the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, reached before her time ran out.
What moved her: You showed the version history with exact dated times and then answered her pasted-draft defence by inviting her to bring the other file, which gave her something she could check and couldn't argue past.
What cost ground: When she asked what you were proposing, you added a third piece of evidence instead of answering, and she got sharper and started objecting to how you ran the meeting.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay's creation just before midnight on a late October night, about as close to that memory as evidence could get; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: The moment she asked what you were putting on the table for Owen, offer 4.4 with a rewrite date before December 1 right then, and keep the writing samples for if she pushes back.
